newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO market consolidates, but Bund spread to narrow.
newsitem.headline: OLO market consolidates, but Bund spread to narrow.

text.p: The yield spread of Belgian 10-year linear bonds (OLOs) over Bunds looks set to move in over the coming months amid buying sentiment, dealers said on Monday.

OLOs are expected to be propped by the view that official interest rates will hold steady for now and that Belgium will succeed in its efforts to be in the first group of countries forming an economic and monetary union in Europe by 1999.

While some traders are setting a target of 17 basis points for the differential, others foresee levels below that. It was at 23 at 1010 GMT on Monday, up two from this morning's level as players took a break from the recent rally and took profits.

The profit-taking in light volumes came after tame U.S. CPI and retail sales data on Friday gave the market another boost. But since there was little concrete news for the market to go on today, moves would be limited, leaving OLOs to track Bunds.
"There is not much direction today, but there are still buyers around," said a trader. The 10-year area was well bid, the benchmark OLO 24 in particular saw reasonable volume.

While for OLOs the downside was limited since domestic accounts -- the main holders of OLOs -- would not sell to take profits, Bunds lacked this cork to float on. Some traders said this too made fresh spread gains for OLOs possible.
Domestic accounts typically hold OLOs for longer-term investment purposes rather than for trading gains.

On EMU, Belgian traders are generally confident the government will be able to slash the budget deficit to the level required in the Maastricht Treaty, thus boosting Belgium's chances to join the single currency.

Little news has emerged on the current negotiations on the 1997 budget, but traders said Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's unbending commitment to EMU meant he would ensure the necessary austerity measures -- estimated at just over 100 billion Belgian francs -- would be taken without fail.
In the run-up to EMU the spread between the countries expected to join is set to narrow.
The OLO/Bund yield differential has come in steadily from the 66 basis point level seen at the end of 1995.
Domestic events in the near term include an exchange auction on Tuesday and a monthly auction next Monday, but these are not expected to move prices, dealers said.
The Bundesbank is due to meet on Thursday, but analysts do not expect any change in the repo rate.
